newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian foreign minister survives attack by gunmen.
newsitem.headline: Haitian foreign minister survives attack by gunmen.

text.p: Gunmen opened fire on a car carrying Haitian Foreign Affairs Minister Fritz Longchamps, but he escaped unharmed, police said on Tuesday.
The assailants shot into the car on a Port-au-Prince street late on Monday, smashing its windows, and fled when the minister's bodyguards returned fire, police said.
"He's lucky because he usually doesn't go around with his security, but last night he did," Haitian National Police spokesman Felder Jean-Baptiste said.
President Rene Preval and his new wife went to visit the minister after the attack, police said.
Last week, Joseph Exume, a former justice minister under ex-President Jean-Bertrand Aristide was shot in the abdomen by attackers who stole his car, Jean-Baptiste said.
Police said there was no evidence linking the two attacks.
The United Nations Security Council was expected to decide soon on a request from Preval to extend the mandate of U.N. peacekeepers by four months. The mandate was scheduled to expire on Thursday.
Haitian officials have said they do not believe the Haitian National Police force, formed shortly after the restoration of democratic rule in the fall of 1994, was ready to maintain the peace.
